Your time toThrive
an inspirational independent school for boys and girls aged 11 to 18.
Year 6 Experience Day (For Year 7 Entry 2027)
Come and have a friendly, no-pressure chat with the team at Sackville School. Tuesday 22nd September 2026 9:00am to 3:00pm Discuss academic and vocational pathways, ask questions and find out how our small classes and personalised mentoring could support your next step. Book your place or simply drop in.
Sackville School promotes a well-rounded and balanced education based on academic, physical, moral and social development for boys and girls aged 11 to 18 years of age.
Our ethos is to provide a positive, friendly, happy, family atmosphere for learning. There is a strong focus on achievement and excellence with an underlying ethos that through hard work and perseverance you can achieve your goals, whether this involves teachers working with each other, parents and staff working together or the students helping and supporting each other.
A look at our prospectus can help provide an initial insight, but there is no substitute for visiting the school for yourself; by talking to the Head, and meeting the pupils and teachers, you will get a real feel of what Sackville School has to offer... Read more
Celebrating the individual
We see each and every pupil as individual with different skills, different passions and different learning styles. To bring out the best in our pupils we help them to discover what these differences are and tailor their learning experience accordingly.
The Sackville family
A sense of community and family underpins all that we do at Sackville. Every pupil will be known to every member of staff, even those they do not have classes with, and can expect to be led, inspired, motivated and cared for while with us.
A traditional education with a tailored approach
The wheel does not always need to be redesigned. At Sackville School we value a traditional academic programme that is tailored to reflect your child’s passions, learning styles and abilities. We supplement this with sports and extra-curricular activities to give your child a well-rounded experience during their time here.
Send the admissions steps to:
We are proud of all of our graduates and of what they achieve during their time here and beyond. Our academic results have always been exceptional and there was a 100% pass rate in 2020 in many subjects including Maths, English, the Sciences, the Humanities and Arts subjects.

Visiting Sackville on a one-to-one basis enables you to truly immerse yourself in the school environment and experience the atmosphere first-hand. It is the best way to observe our school in action; hearing directly from both pupils and staff will provide insight into whether our school is the right fit for you and your child.
At Sackville, we are always delighted to welcome prospective parents. We can arrange a personal tour for you, during which you will have the opportunity to meet our Headteacher, explore our school community, and familiarise yourself with our facilities and staff.
With immediate places available and September 2026 entry now open, there has never been a better time to discover all that Sackville has to offer.
To book a personal tour, please fill out the form below, and a member of our Admissions Team will be in contact with you shortly.
Alternatively, if you are interested in our upcoming Open Days, please click here to check for scheduled events.
Personal Tours & Visits

Pastoral Care at Sackville School
At Sackville School, pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do. We believe that students thrive when they feel safe, valued, and supported — both academically and personally. Our pastoral system is designed to ensure every young person is known as an individual and receives the guidance they need to flourish. Staff work closely to support pupils with their individual learning plans to ensure every child receives a bespoke educational experience.
Each student is part of a supportive tutor group, led by experienced staff who build strong, lasting relationships with pupils and their families. Heads of Year and pastoral support teams work closely together to provide a nurturing environment where students feel confident to face challenges, celebrate success, and develop resilience.
We are proud of our inclusive and caring community, where kindness, respect, and wellbeing are promoted daily. Whether a student is navigating personal challenges, academic pressure, or simply needs someone to talk to, they can count on Sackville to be a safe and supportive space.
The ISI report noted the strength of the school’s PSHE and RSE programmes, careers education from Year 7, and effective SEND and safeguarding provision. The school has enhanced systems for leadership, pupil welfare and safety
“We’ve seen such a positive difference in our child since joining Sackville. The care and attention from staff is exceptional. It’s a school that really sees and supports the whole child — not just exam results.”
“There’s a genuine sense of community and purpose here. Our small classes allow us to know each pupil as an individual and tailor support in ways that truly make a difference. It’s a privilege to be part of their journey.”
This report reflects strength and growth for Sackville School as it continues to offer a distinctive and forward-thinking educational experience in the heart of Kent.
The Wellbeing Hub at Sackville School
Our Wellbeing Hub is a dedicated space where every student is welcome and supported. Open to all year groups, the hub offers a calm, safe environment where pupils can access the help they need — whether it's a quick check-in or ongoing support.
Through one-to-one sessions, walk and talk meetings, and both pastoral and academic guidance, students can speak openly with trusted adults who are trained to listen, understand, and offer meaningful support. The Wellbeing Hub plays a key role in ensuring every pupil’s voice is heard and that no concern goes unnoticed.
At Sackville, we believe that wellbeing is the foundation for success. The hub is just one of the many ways we care for our students beyond the classroom, helping them to thrive both personally and academically.

Discover Life at Sackville School
Is your child currently in Year 6 and preparing for the exciting transition to secondary education?
Join us for our Rainforest-themed Year 6 Experience Day and give your child the opportunity to experience a typical day at Sackville School.
Throughout the day, pupils will enjoy engaging lessons and rainforest-inspired activities, meet our teachers, make new friends and explore our excellent facilities.

Experience the Sackville Difference
We warmly invite prospective families to join us for one of our Open Mornings and discover everything Sackville School has to offer.
Meet our Head, teachers and pupils, explore our facilities and gain a first-hand insight into daily life at the school. Choosing the right Sixth Form is one of the most important decisions a young person will make.
Join us for our Sixth Form Information Evening and discover how Sackville School helps students achieve outstanding academic outcomes while preparing confidently for university, apprenticeships and future careers.
Meet our Sixth Form team, explore our subject options, learn about our personalised mentoring and careers guidance programme, and hear how we support every student to achieve their ambitions.

Reserve your place today and take the next step towards a successful future.

That’s why we offer personal tours throughout the year, giving you the opportunity to visit at a time that suits you. Experience the school in action, meet our teachers, and see how your child would thrive in a calm, nurturing environment. It’s a more personal, relaxed way to discover what makes our school special — and to ask the questions that matter most to you.
Book your personal tour today and see the difference for yourself.

Please complete this form to request a Prospectus Pack to be posted to you. Our Admission Team will then be in contact to talk through next steps.
Data Protection
In accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) 2018, we hereby wish to notify you of how we intend to use the information you are providing on this form. The data you have provided will be stored by Sackville School (the School) for the purposes of communicating with you as you progress through our admissions process. The data we have requested is justified as the first stage in progressing your potential application and as a legitimate interest. Your data will be kept indefinitely or until such a time as you ask for it to be deleted. Your data will not be shared with anyone outside of the School except for the processing of your potential application. Communication may include letters, emails, telephone calls and newsletters. If you believe we have misused your data, you have the right to complain to the ICO. By submitting this form, you are acknowledging that you have read and understood this information and give consent for us to hold your data.

In order to develop well-rounded and capable people, we offer varied school sports and extra-curricular activities as an essential part of your child’s education. Sport is a significant aspect of life at Sackville, where we offer a varied programme throughout the school in PE and Games lessons.
Our main team sports are football, cricket, rugby, hockey, netball, basketball and volleyball. We arrange fixtures with other schools most weeks and look to develop team captains from all year groups.
Education that goes beyond the classroom.
As well as clubs and societies throughout the week, on a Friday afternoon for Years 7-9 we have our activity sessions further extend your child’s passions. Options include horse riding, fencing, swimming, climbing, trampolining, and mountain biking, among many other activities. We are also a licenced Duke of Edinburgh Centre and from Year 9 your child can enrol on the Bronze award.
We also offer a fantastic range of hands-on learning experiences, from bringing in renowned speakers, authors or athletes, to school trips to experience plenty of cultural opportunities. These invaluably help supplement classroom learning across many subjects, including: English, Drama, Humanities, Languages, Music, PE, Mathematics, and Science.

pageCache.pageTitle: More Conversation. Less Scrolling | Sackville School
pageCache.text:
At Sackville School, we believe young people need space to focus, build genuine friendships and be fully present.
Since 2023, our mobile phone-free school day has created an environment where pupils can learn, socialise and develop without the constant distraction of smartphones. Staff have seen first-hand the positive difference this can make to wellbeing, relationships, confidence and engagement in lessons.
As national conversations continue around children's access to social media and the impact of smartphones on young people's lives, Sackville's experience offers a powerful insight into what can happen when pupils are given meaningful time away from their devices.
Our approach has also attracted wider attention and was recently featured in local press, highlighting the positive impact Sackville's phone-free school day has had on pupil wellbeing, relationships and engagement.
Phone-Free Since 2023
Sackville introduced its mobile phone-free school day in 2023, recognising the growing impact that smartphones and social media were having on young people's wellbeing, concentration and relationships.
Originally introduced by Deputy Head Kate Kirkpatrick, the initiative has continued to evolve under the leadership of Headteacher Leoni Ellis and remains a central part of our commitment to pupil wellbeing.
The approach is simple: during the school day, pupils are given genuine space away from their phones.
Space to focus on learning. Space to talk. Space to build friendships. Space to be present.
Since introducing the policy, staff have observed calmer break times, more face-to-face conversation, increased social interaction, improved lesson engagement and a stronger sense of community throughout the school.
More Face-to-Face Interaction. Greater Focus.
One of the most noticeable changes has been the way pupils interact throughout the school day. Without the constant pull of notifications, messages and social media, break times and lunchtimes become opportunities for genuine conversation, laughter and connection.
Removing mobile phones from the school day also creates an environment with fewer distractions and greater opportunities for pupils to focus fully on learning, contribute to discussions and solve problems together.
"One of the greatest benefits has been seeing pupils simply talking to one another again. Break times and lunchtimes are filled with conversation, laughter and genuine interaction. These everyday moments are vital to young people's social and emotional development." -Leoni Ellis, Headteacher
Not Anti-Technology. Pro-Balance.
Our approach is not about rejecting technology. Technology plays an important role in education, future careers and modern life.
Instead, we believe young people should be supported to develop a healthy and balanced relationship with their devices.
Young people today are growing up in a world of constant notifications, updates and digital stimulation. By removing mobile phones from the school day, Sackville creates a valuable break from that constant digital pull and more opportunities for pupils to concentrate, build confidence and develop real-world social skills.
"This has never been about being anti-technology. It is about helping young people develop a healthy relationship with their devices and ensuring school remains a place where they can focus, learn and grow." -Leoni Ellis, Headteacher
An Approach Attracting Wider Interest
Sackville's mobile phone-free school day has attracted wider political and media interest, including a visit from local MP Tom Tugendhat, who met staff and pupils to learn more about the impact of the policy on school culture and wellbeing.
The school's approach has also been featured in the media as the national conversation around young people's use of smartphones and social media continues to grow.
For us, however, the greatest measure of success is found in the everyday moments across our school: pupils talking together at break, engaging fully in lessons, solving problems collaboratively and building the confidence to communicate face to face.
A School Where Every Child Is Known
Our mobile phone-free school day reflects Sackville's wider educational philosophy: creating an environment where every child is known, valued and encouraged to flourish.
As an independent co-educational school in Hildenborough for pupils aged 11 to 18, Sackville combines small class sizes, individual attention and strong pastoral care with an education designed to help young people grow in confidence, independence and ambition.
"Our experience shows that when young people are given opportunities to disconnect from their devices and reconnect with each other, the benefits are significant." -Leoni Ellis, Headteacher
See the Difference for Yourself
Choosing a school is about much more than what you can read online. It is about experiencing the atmosphere, meeting the teachers and pupils, and seeing whether it feels like the right environment for your child.
We invite families to visit Sackville, explore our school, meet our staff and pupils, and discover how our personal approach to education helps young people thrive.
Come and experience a school with more conversation, stronger connections and space for every child to flourish.
Read more about Sackville's phone-free school day and its impact on pupils in our recent local press coverage
Book your place at an Open Day or arrange a personal visit to Sackville School here.
About Sackville

We are seeking a passionate and dedicated Maths Teacher to join our team of exceptional educators. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Maths education, a love for teaching, and the ability to create engaging and dynamic Maths lessons.
About Sackville School
Sackville is a thriving independent senior school (11-18) of 220 boys and girls. Sackville offers an ambitious education that is individually tailored for each pupil to realise their potential. We are a welcoming school with a warm sense of community. Our academic outcomes are excellent, particularly our ability to add value to each and every pupil.
Sackville School aims to foster a positive, friendly, happy, family atmosphere for learning. This is a powerful and integral element of our school’s success and requires careful cultivation from teachers, staff, and leaders alike. To achieve the most from our pupils we understand that enjoyment of learning is of paramount importance. Children learn best when both they and their teachers, are enjoying themselves.
We aim to encourage intellectual curiosity and productive learning habits in both our students and staff. Whether you are fully trained or seeking further qualifications, we have many opportunities for you to broaden your skill set and reach your career goals.
Sackville School is part of the leading academic group, Alpha Schools. Alpha is recognised within the education field as an established and award-winning network of independent schools from across the country. Strong collaboration across the group builds opportunities for our pupils and staff as we work together to offer a high-quality education within a stimulating environment.
Do you have the passion to roll-up your sleeves and get stuck-in to every aspect of our school? If you can honestly say yes to this question, we would like to meet you.
Please note that CVs are welcome but will not be considered without a completed Sackville application form.
We reserve the right to close advertisements early if a suitable candidate is found.
No Recruitment Agencies please.

Data Protection
In accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) 2018, we hereby wish to notify you of how we intend to use the information you are providing on this form. The data you have provided will be stored by Sackville School (the School) for the purposes of communicating with you as you progress through our admissions process. The data we have requested is justified as the first stage in progressing your potential application and as a legitimate interest. Your data will be kept indefinitely or until such a time as you ask for it to be deleted. Your data will not be shared with anyone outside of the School except for the processing of your potential application. Communication may include letters, emails, telephone calls and newsletters. If you believe we have misused your data, you have the right to complain to the ICO. By submitting this form, you are acknowledging that you have read and understood this information and give consent for us to hold your data.
